newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA HALFWAY TO ONE MILLION HOUSING TARGET.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA HALFWAY TO ONE MILLION HOUSING TARGET.

text.p: South Africa has delivered more than half of the one million houses promised by President Nelson Mandela during his campaign for the first democratic elections in 1994, the housing minister said on Wednesday.
Housing Minister Sankie Mthembe-Mahanyele told parliament her department had approved 555,000 housing subsidies by mid-April.
She said 192,815 houses had been built or were under construction as a result of subsidies already paid out in 805 housing projects around the country.
"This is delivery in action and shows we are keeping our promise to house the nation," she said.
More than seven million South Africans live in informal shanties and the official housing backlog tops two million units.

Mandela's African National Congress (ANC), which won 62 percent of the vote in the country's first all-race elections in April 1994, promised to build a million houses during its first five years in power.
The ANC has come under fire this year for failing to deliver on election promises including housing.

The government conceded soon after coming into power that it could not physically build and deliver a million houses and, instead, implemented a subsidy scheme offering up to 15,000 rand to the poorest families.

About half the subsidy goes towards the cost of serviced plots and the rest is available for basic structures. Some projects include private-sector loans to bolster the subsidies. - Parliament newsroom +27 21 4032502
